text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt a single 4px #005fcc focus ring with a 2px white box-shadow blur on every interactive element. This keeps the ring visible against any background while avoiding the complexity of stacking two rings. The trade-off is slightly softer edges on high-contrast backgrounds, but the blur ensures clarity without visual noise.

name: Reader
text: The single 4px ring with white blur may not be enough, as it fails on high-contrast mode and the white shadow can get lost. A better alternative would be to use a high-contrast outline that adapts to the background, ensuring the focus ring remains visible in all modes. To settle the argument, we need to test the proposed solution with users who rely on high-contrast mode and verify that our chosen approach meets the accessibility standards.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a double focus ring: 4px #005fcc solid ring with a 2px solid white inner ring. This guarantees visibility against every background, including high-contrast mode, without relying on blur that can soften edges. The trade-off is slightly more CSS, but it’s a one-line rule that never fails the user.

name: Reader
text: The double ring risks visual clutter on small or dense interfaces, where the inner white ring may shrink to invisibility or compete with nearby elements. A safer alternative is a single 2px high-contrast outline (e.g., white on dark or black on light) with a 2px solid fallback color, tested in both normal and high-contrast modes. Settle it by testing on a live EXCAVA component under pinch-zoom and forced colors mode.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Adopt a single 4px #005fcc focus ring with a 2px solid white inset shadow on all interactive elements. The result must deliver a high-contrast, keyboard-navigable focus indicator that works in all modes (including high-contrast) without visual clutter. Owner: Ramp.
